title: Canonical projective quotient augmentation, Roos model and completeness
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and put $A_n=R/\pi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $\underline M_T$ for the constant sheaf of an $R$-module $M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$, with projections $\operatorname{pr}_{T,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a specified bounded complex of finite projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and put $M_T^\bullet=B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{P^\bullet}_T$ and $D_{T,n}^\bullet=(A_n)_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{P^\bullet}_T$, with the given scalar differentials [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Use sheaves of modules and their ambient unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Restrict $D_{T,n}^\bullet$ to $B_T$ along $\operatorname{pr}_{T,n}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and use the strict transitions $q_{n+1,n}\otimes1$. Write $F^\bullet=\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_{T,n}^\bullet$ for the termwise product and $u=1-s:F^\bullet\to F^\bullet$, where $s((x_n)_n)=(q_{n+1,n}(x_{n+1}))_n$. The quotient maps $\alpha_n:M_T^\bullet\to\operatorname{Res}_nD_{T,n}^\bullet$, $b\otimes p\mapsto\operatorname{pr}_{T,n}(b)\otimes p$, make $M_T^\bullet$ the ordinary limit complex. In every degree these cones and diagrams are compatible split retracts of finite powers of the completed coefficient cone, with degree-dependent ranks, and there is a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow M_T^r\xrightarrow{(\alpha_n^r)_n}F^r\xrightarrow{u^r}F^r\longrightarrow0.$$

In the strict cochain mapping-cone convention, put $\mathsf C(D)=\operatorname{Cone}(u)[-1]$ [def-weil-derived-limit]. The chain map $\beta:M_T^\bullet\to\mathsf C(D)$ whose unshifted-product component is $(\alpha_n)_n$ and whose shifted-product component is zero is degreewise monic; its cokernel is isomorphic as a complex to $\operatorname{Cone}(1_{F^\bullet})[-1]$ and is contractible. Thus the canonical strict augmentation induces an isomorphism
$$[M_T^\bullet]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_{T,n}^\bullet$$
in $D(B_T)$, where the right side is the total derived limit of the strict tower [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Under the normalized comparison of the Roos-cone and K-injective tower models [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], it is exactly $[\beta]$. Its composite with every derived-limit projection is $[\alpha_n]$. These statements are natural in all scalar chain maps; no selection of maps between unrelated triangulated cones is made.

Moreover $[M_T^\bullet]$ is locally derived $(\pi)B_T$-complete: on every slice $U$ and every local section $b$ of $\pi B_T$, $R\mathcal Hom(B_U[1/b],M_T^\bullet|_U)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. It is derived complete in the Roos-triangle convention [def-weil-derived-complete], and its specified intrinsic product-fibre completion unit is invertible [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. All assertions hold without any finiteness hypothesis on $T$.

proof.text: For each degree $r$, choose generators of $P^r$ and the resulting surjection $R^{d_r}\to P^r$; projectivity lifts $1_{P^r}$ to a section, giving $i_r:P^r\to R^{d_r}$ and $p_r:R^{d_r}\to P^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$. Constant realization and tensoring preserve this equation. The free-module tensor identification sends $b\otimes(a_j)_j$ to $(ba_j)_j$, with inverse $(b_j)_j\mapsto\sum_jb_j\otimes e_j$; the formulas hold locally for constant sections and sheafify. Thus the quotient cones for $P^r$ are compatible retracts of the $d_r$-fold coefficient cone, with idempotent $i_rp_r$ at every level. Limits are sectionwise. A compatible family in this retract is a family in $(\lim_n(A_n)_T)^{d_r}=B_T^{d_r}$ fixed by this same idempotent, whose image is exactly $M_T^r$. Its projections are $\alpha_n^r$. Hence $M_T^r=\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_{T,n}^r$, canonically. Since $\alpha_n^{r+1}d=d\alpha_n^r$, these identifications assemble into the ordinary limit complex. No splitting of the differentials is asserted.

The actual projections $B_T\to(A_n)_T$ are epimorphisms by [lem-sp-completed-coefficient-regular-quotients]. Since $q_{n+1,n}\operatorname{pr}_{T,n+1}=\operatorname{pr}_{T,n}$, each $q_{n+1,n}$ is epic. Finite powers and their compatible retracts remain epic: lift after including in the free target and then apply the source retraction. Thus the transitions of each sheaf tower $\operatorname{Res}_nD_{T,n}^r$ are epic. Apply clause 1 of [lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit] with coefficient ring sheaf $B_T$. Its kernel is the limit computed in Step 1, and its map is precisely $u^r=1-s$, proving the displayed short exact sequence in every degree.

proof.text: In coordinates $(y,x)\in F^{r-1}\oplus F^r$, the strict fiber differential is $(-dy-ux,dx)$. Therefore $\beta(m)=(0,\alpha m)$ is a chain map and monic. The map $(y,x)\mapsto(y,ux)$ to $Z^r=F^{r-1}\oplus F^r$ with differential $(-dy-z,dz)$ is epic, has kernel $\beta(M^r)$, and commutes with differentials because $du=ud$. It identifies the cokernel complex with $Z=\operatorname{Cone}(1_F)[-1]$. On $Z$, $h(y,z)=(0,-y)$ gives $dh+hd=(y,z)$, proving contractibility. Apply [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] to the degreewise epimorphism $u$ to conclude that this very $\beta$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Countable products of $B_T$-module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Thus [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] applies to this strict tower and gives $\rho_D:\mathsf C(D)\simeq R\lim D$. Its strict-augmentation clause identifies $\rho_D[\beta]$ with the canonical augmentation, and its projection clause makes its $n$th projection $[\alpha_n]$. Hence this canonical augmentation is invertible. For any scalar chain map $f:P\to Q$, the equality $(1\otimes f)\alpha_n^P=\alpha_n^Q(1\otimes f)$ follows on $b\otimes p$ by taking the same residue of $b$ on either side. The induced map on both product coordinates commutes with $u$ and $\beta$; naturality of $\rho$ proves all the asserted naturalities.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, normalized strict augmentation comparison; exact products from Bhatt-Scholze Proposition 3.1.9

proof.text: Each $M_T^r$ is flat: tensoring with it is a retract, using Step 1, of a finite direct sum of identity functors; the homology of the tensor of a short exact sequence is accordingly a retract of zero. Thus boundedness and [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] make $M_T^\bullet$ K-flat. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], its derived reductions are computed by ordinary tensor with $(A_n)_T$. The balancing isomorphism $(b\otimes p)\otimes a\mapsto\operatorname{pr}_{T,n}(b)a\otimes p$, with inverse $a\otimes p\mapsto(1\otimes p)\otimes a$, identifies these reductions, their quotient units and transitions with the specified $D_{T,n}$. Consequently the strict fiber triangle transported along $[\beta]$ is the Roos triangle required by [def-weil-derived-complete], with its first arrow exactly $(\alpha_n)_n$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; ordinary tensor computation of derived scalar extension and the definition of the Roos-triangle condition

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-roos-intrinsic-unit-comparison] to this flat-term K-flat representative. Its equality $d_K\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}=\operatorname{comp}_K$ and invertibility of $d_K$ and of the augmentation from Step 4, transported along the Step 5 identification $U_n\cong D_{T,n}$, prove that the specified intrinsic unit is invertible. Its coordinate map $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$ identifies the intrinsic fiber unit with the degree-zero Koszul unit $\eta_V$, which is therefore invertible. Since $M_T^\bullet$ is K-flat, $M_T^\bullet\otimes^L Q_m$ is represented by the strict tower $V_m=M_T^\bullet\otimes_{B_T}[B_T\xrightarrow{\pi^m}B_T]$; the strict-augmentation clause of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies $\rho_V\eta_V$ with the canonical derived Koszul unit $M_T^\bullet\to R\lim_m(M_T^\bullet\otimes^LQ_m)$, which is thus invertible. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] over $B_T$ with the single global generator $\pi$: its unit is invertible if and only if the object is locally derived $\pi B_T$-complete. This gives the required vanishing for every slice $U$ and every $b\in(\pi B_T)(U)$, including sections that are only locally divisible by $\pi$. All the cited inputs allow arbitrary schemes; boundedness was used only for the K-flat calculation.
